subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw add enforced execution anti-drift guards in core, and what state, timer, and rollout scope should be allowed?
rationale: The request is not a narrow bug fix: it changes execution policy, persistence, telemetry, status delivery, and configuration defaults, and the repository policy pushes runtime state toward SQLite rather than the requested file shape.

options.title: Design a narrow core guard
options.body: Approve a bounded design using existing agent/cron lifecycle events, SQLite state, conservative timers, telemetry, and focused proof before implementation.

options.title: Keep partial guards only
options.body: Leave current tool-loop, idle-timeout, strict-agentic, and cron acknowledgement protections as the supported behavior and close or narrow this umbrella later.

options.title: Defer to an external workflow
options.body: Treat post-green follow-through and operator escalation as workflow automation outside core unless a missing OpenClaw extension API is identified.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow core guard
recommendation.body: Approve a bounded design using existing agent/cron lifecycle events, SQLite state, conservative timers, telemetry, and focused proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest recent routing signal for the current agent/cron guard surfaces and can sponsor or reject the broad core policy direction.
